title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned a film-lab leader. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Film laboratory leader
options.thesis: The shelf is a reel you thread: books, films, and games as frames on one strip.
options.viewport: A full-bleed gate: r4t5 as the slate, three reel bands, the first one already inked blue.
options.risk: A title sequence can bury the chapters if the reels are not the largest thing on screen.

raised.raise: One continuous strip. Chapters pin to frame numbers, not to separate cards.
A blue void sits between chapter blocks so each reel reads as a cut mass.
One handwritten blue note on the slate, so the bench looks used.
The frame counter advances with the reading and always shows where now is.

options.label: Night index catalog
options.thesis: Each work is a cobalt tab in a black drawer. You pull a card and read why it stays.
options.viewport: Three drawer fronts. The books drawer is pulled open, cards fanned.
options.risk: Also the direction most personal library sites land on.

options.label: Patent drawing sheet
options.thesis: Each favorite is a numbered figure. A leader line ties the title to the sentence that keeps it.
options.viewport: One sheet. Fig. 1 is a book, its leader pulled taut to the claim.
options.case: Holds clarity: the reason for each work is a labeled part. Loses identification: a patent is a machine, not a night shelf.
options.risk: The page can feel like a diagram of taste instead of a place to read.

options.label: Depot destination blind
options.thesis: Books, films, and games are three destinations under one window. You step the blind to the reel you want.
options.viewport: One fixed window. BOOKS is stepped into place in blue on black.
options.case: Holds wayfinding: three destinations, one window. Loses identification: a timetable is not a private reading bench.
options.risk: The flap can shout the names and leave no room for the essays.

options.label: Daylight section
options.case: A sunbeam through rooms does not name books, films, or games, and daylight fights a night shelf.
options.kept: One continuous ruled section, annotations pinned to a path.

options.label: Cloud quarry
options.case: Cutting weather does not explain a personal canon, and the audience does not live in a quarry.
options.kept: Deep gaps between masses, so sections breathe.

options.label: Club sleeve scrawl
options.case: A 4 a.m. party photo hides the essays, and a reading visitor does not identify with the club.
options.kept: One handled mark, so the surface looks used.

options.label: Drum-machine step row
options.case: Sixteen steps do not map onto three essays, and a sequencer is not how this visitor reads.
options.kept: A chase that always shows where now is.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark personal page: a name, a short intro, and three equal content blocks.
canonCard.viewport: Name at the top, three matching cards for books, films, and games.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dark personal site.
